hypothesis: Under the deliberately favorable assumption of equal constants and no lower-order overhead, the corollary exponent delta=1e-13 supplies at least a 1 percent operation-count reduction for Fourier lengths 2^k with k between 4 and 40.
baseline: n*ln(n); favorable proxy n*ln(n)^(1-delta), neither is a measured implementation
judge: 70-digit Decimal calculation of exp(-delta*ln(ln(n))) and exact integer lower storage calculation for W*=2^71 scalar slots
failure: favorable proxy still falls below 1 percent at every declared n
limits: A numerical applicability screen, not an FFT implementation, speed benchmark, general lower bound, or falsification of the theorem. Big-O constants and log-log factors are excluded favorably.
